runtime_compatibility.notes: Validated against current main branch runtime in dry-run mode.

entries.name: learn/hello
entries.intent: Say hello in a creative way — the simplest orchestration.
entries.description: Say hello in a creative way — the simplest orchestration.

entries.name: learn/prompt
entries.intent: prompt primitive — text, json, number, boolean output types
entries.description: Template: basic prompt with text, json, number, and boolean outputs.

entries.name: learn/dynamic_chain
entries.intent: dynamic primitive — chain flow (sequential, each step sees prior outputs)
entries.description: Template: dynamic chain — sequential multi-step pipeline.

entries.name: learn/dynamic_tree
entries.intent: dynamic primitive — tree flow (all steps share the same input snapshot)
entries.description: Template: dynamic tree — parallel fan-out execution.

entries.name: learn/conditional
entries.intent: if primitive — deterministic CEL branching
entries.description: Template: if/then/else branching with CEL expressions.

entries.name: learn/loop
entries.intent: loop primitive — each iteration over a JSON array
entries.description: Template: loop with each/as iteration and tree parallelism.

entries.name: learn/reflector
entries.intent: reflector primitive — runtime effect generation
entries.description: Template: reflector — runtime plan generation and execution.

entries.name: learn/cyberdiner_hello
entries.intent: cyberdiner adapter — send one prompt through the CyberDiner job queue at the cheap tier.
entries.description: Minimal prompt orchestration pinned to the cyberdiner adapter. `model:` names a capability tier (cheap, fast, good, good-fast, alpha …) rather than a provider model; the submit/poll job queue is handled inside the adapter.
entries.when_to_use: When you want to see how an orchestration targets the CyberDiner broker, or as the starting point for one. Requires `runtime.adapters.cyberdiner.expo_url` and `token` in config — never in the YAML.

answer.description: Two-sentence answer returned by the cook serving that tier.

entries.example: cof run learn/cyberdiner_hello -e question="What is cybernetics?"

entries.name: utilities/summarize
entries.intent: Compress text into a single concise sentence.
entries.description: Single-pass distillation of a text input down to one sentence.
entries.when_to_use: When a downstream effect needs a one-line gist of a longer passage.

entries.name: utilities/critique
entries.intent: Return a structured critique with score, issues, and strengths.
entries.description: Reviews content against named criteria; returns JSON with score, issues, strengths.
entries.when_to_use: Pair with utilities/refine to drive a critique→refine loop.

entries.name: utilities/refine
entries.intent: Revise content guided by reviewer feedback.
entries.description: Applies feedback (typically from critique.yml) to revise content while preserving voice.
entries.when_to_use: Pair with utilities/critique inside a feedback loop.

entries.name: utilities/judge
entries.intent: Pick the best candidate from a list against a stated objective.
entries.description: Selects one candidate by zero-based index and returns a one-sentence rationale.
entries.when_to_use: Collapse N parallel attempts (e.g. from a tree-loop) into a single chosen output.

candidates.description: JSON-stringified array or numbered text block.

entries.name: utilities/classify
entries.intent: Assign one label from a fixed set to a piece of content.
entries.description: Returns the chosen label (verbatim from the input set) plus a 0–1 confidence.
entries.when_to_use: Routing the orchestration based on content type — intent classification, triage.

entries.name: utilities/decompose
entries.intent: Break a high-level task into an ordered array of subtasks.
entries.description: Returns a JSON array of imperative subtask sentences.
entries.when_to_use: Plan the iteration array for a downstream loop(each).

entries.name: utilities/extract
entries.intent: Pull named fields out of unstructured text into a typed object.
entries.description: Returns an object whose keys exactly match the requested field names. Missing values are null.
entries.when_to_use: Turn prose (email, transcript) into structured data for downstream effects.

entries.name: utilities/route
entries.intent: Pick a route key from a {key, description} map for given content.
entries.description: Returns the chosen route key (verbatim from the input). Combine with `if` to dispatch.
entries.when_to_use: Multi-arm dispatch where each route maps to a specialised follow-up.

entries.name: patterns/all_primitives
entries.intent: all primitives composed — dynamic, loop, if, prompt, use
entries.description: Template: all primitives composed — dynamic, loop, conditional, prompt, use.

entries.name: patterns/critique_refine_loop
entries.intent: Iterate critique → refine until the model judges the draft good enough.
entries.description: loop(while, mode: model) wrapping use:utilities/critique and use:utilities/refine.

entries.name: patterns/parallel_then_judge
entries.intent: Generate N candidate variants in parallel, then judge the best.
entries.description: loop(each, flow: tree, collect:) → use:utilities/judge.

entries.name: patterns/classify_then_route
entries.intent: Classify a query, then dispatch to one of three branches via if.
entries.description: use:utilities/classify followed by chained if/else for branch dispatch.

entries.name: recipes/article_summarizer
entries.intent: Summarize an article into a concise one-sentence summary.
entries.description: Summarize an article into a concise one-sentence summary.

article_text.description: Full text of the article to summarize.

max_words.description: Maximum words for the final summary (default model decides).

entries.name: recipes/comic_strip
entries.intent: Generate a 2–4 panel comic strip with AI art and text overlays.
entries.description: Generate a 2–4 panel comic strip with AI art and text overlays.

prompt.description: Premise or theme for the comic strip.

entries.example: cof run recipes/comic_strip -e prompt='a cat discovers gravity'

entries.name: recipes/research_brief
entries.intent: Decompose a topic into sub-questions, gather answers in parallel, synthesise a brief, then self-critique.
entries.description: Composes utilities/decompose, a parallel loop(tree)+collect, and utilities/critique.

entries.name: recipes/code_review
entries.intent: Review a unified-diff hunk and emit issues with severity, line, category, suggestion.
entries.description: Pulls metadata via utilities/extract, then a single structured-output review pass.

entries.name: recipes/meeting_notes
entries.intent: Transcript → structured notes: TL;DR, attendees, decisions, action items.
entries.description: Composes utilities/summarize and utilities/extract in a parallel dynamic, then a structured pass for decisions and action items.

entries.name: agents/meta_orchestrator
entries.intent: Generate a new orchestration from a natural language prompt.
entries.description: Generate a new orchestration from a natural language prompt.

user_request.description: Natural language description of the orchestration to build.

entries.example: cof gen my-orch 'Build an article summarizer'

entries.name: agents/improver
entries.intent: Analyze and improve an existing orchestration YAML.
entries.description: Analyze and improve an existing orchestration YAML.

original_prompt.description: The original intent the orchestration was built for.

rules.description: LLM authoring rules (auto-injected by improve-orchestration script).

entries.name: agents/improver_judge
entries.intent: Convergence judge — decides if two orchestration versions have converged.
entries.description: Convergence judge — decides if two orchestration versions have converged.

entries.name: agents/wizard
entries.intent: Conversational wizard — one turn of an interview that drafts and self-validates an orchestration.
entries.description: Handles ONE turn of a conversation that builds an orchestration: interprets the transcript, either asks a clarifying question or drafts the target YAML, validates the draft with the validate_yaml tool, and revises it in a bounded loop until it passes. The host drives the outer conversation loop.
entries.when_to_use: When a human wants to build an orchestration by talking rather than by writing YAML. Drive it from a chat view or a Python loop over api.run_orchestration.

goal.description: What the human wants the target orchestration to do.

conversation.description: Prior turns, oldest first; each item is a {role, content} object. Empty on the first turn.

draft.description: The current orchestration YAML, or empty if none exists yet.

say.description: The wizard's message to the human for this turn.

yaml.description: The validated orchestration YAML; null on a question turn.

done.description: True only when the wizard is finished AND the draft is valid.

valid.description: Whether this turn's draft validated; null on a question turn.

errors.description: Validator errors for this turn's draft, if any.
